children: Mayville Engineering reported third-quarter 2026 net sales of $170.4 million, up 18.1% year over year, and net income of $0.4 million, compared with a $2.7 million loss a year earlier. Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.15, while Adjusted EBITDA was $17.0 million. The company cited accelerating Datacenter & Critical Power demand and improving capacity utilization.
Net sales were $170.4 million, an 18.1% increase from $144.3 million in the prior-year quarter.
Manufacturing margin was $18.8 million, or 11.0% of net sales, compared with $15.9 million and 11.0% a year earlier.
Income from operations was $4.3 million, versus $48,000 in the third quarter of 2025.
Net income was $0.4 million, or $0.02 per diluted share, compared with a net loss of $2.7 million, or $0.13 per diluted share. Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.15.
Adjusted EBITDA was $17.0 million, or 10.0% of net sales, compared with $14.1 million and 9.8% a year earlier.

Datacenter & Critical Power demand accelerated, supported by legacy customers and new project launches. MEC secured approximately $45 million in project awards during the quarter, and its qualified opportunity pipeline exceeded $200 million.

Commercial Vehicle and Construction & Access demand improved, while Powersports and Agriculture remained soft. Military programs faced continued transition delays, and Other markets benefited from aluminum extrusion demand.
MEC expects awarded programs and its opportunity pipeline to bring the company to full capacity within 18 months and has begun deploying capital to expand its footprint.

The company closed on its Thomson, Georgia facility on October 1. Together with planned equipment investment, the facility is expected to add approximately $50 million of annual revenue capacity by 2028 and raise total capacity above the previously disclosed approximately $850 million.

Management said project launch and outsourcing costs, premium labor, and alignment of operations with customer timelines are expected to remain factors over the coming quarters as Datacenter & Critical Power volumes ramp.
